top_rigor_problems: Engine cuts that change meaning, not just flow: removed sentences leave a phrase attributed to the wrong bishop (F1-T, Cyprian's 'contagion of the ancient death' given to Augustine, his hard teaching on unbaptized infants dropped) or a pronoun that reads as God (F1-I).
Voice over-reach past the record: an invented Fussala attribution for the apse letter (F5-E), and Felicissimus made a 'rival bishop' with a causal claim the record says not to state as fact (F3-P).
A false denial and a prompt leak: F4-T says the record does not speak of rebirth when two records do ('not regenerated', 'born of God'); F2-E recites citation rules instead of answering.
top_access_problems: Orphan pronouns and dangling lead-ins from cut sentences in about a third of answers ('he wrote that down years afterward', 'The same voice that taught also warned', 'a rule he would not break', 'Yet in that same letter').

Build or system talk reaching participants: 'this turn', 'this turn's evidence block', 'verified in this build', 'I am a representative of Latin Pastoral-Congregational Christianity', 'Looking at what we have to tell from'.
Chatbot cadence and recycled passages: 'The short answer first. Yes.' (F4-P); the same restless-heart and pattern-of-the-cross paragraphs reused word for word across C-I, C-P, C-T, F1-P and F4-P.
world_summary.cost_note: Most answers are 110-260 words and cost about $0.02-0.03. Longer than their value: F3-I (839 words, ~550 beyond need; 1,743 output tokens, the most of any answer), C-E (474 words, ~220 beyond), F2-E (355 words, ~180 of prompt recital), F4-T (~110 beyond) and F1-I (~90). C-I cost $0.12 with no cache read, about four times the others; this is input-side, not length. Trimming F3-I and C-E to the question would save most of the excess output tokens.
world_summary.go_live_view: Not yet. The record base is strong and honest: the honest-limit answers (F3-E, F4-E, F5-I) and the core doctrinal ones (F2-T, F5-T, F6-I) are good, and 22 of 28 answers are scholarly acceptable. But 6 BLOCKs and 11 FIXes are too many for participants, and most share one cause: the engine's sentence cutting leaves orphan pronouns, missing referents and, twice, wrong attributions. The single most valuable fix is to make the cut step repair or drop the dependent sentences around a cut (or to re-check the output for orphan 'he/they/that/Yet' and announced-but-missing content). That would clear most FIXes and two BLOCKs. Next, strip build vocabulary ('this turn', 'build', citation rules) before output, and add 'born again/regenerated' retrieval to F4-T.
